cases.name: A new match can answer the wrong question
cases.description: The first question selects a two-edge path through a loop's upper corner at a site between the path endpoints. A separate lower path has an endpoint join. Searching afresh answers Yes using that other path; retaining the selected path answers No.
cases.initialQuestion: Select a two-edge straight path whose site between its endpoints joins the loop's upper corner.
cases.followupQuestion: Does an endpoint of the selected two-edge path join a three-edge loop?

cases.name: Keep the path while allowing a new partner
cases.description: The selected path contacts the first loop at a site between its endpoints, and another loop through its right endpoint. Only the path role is retained. The loop role may find a different partner, so the follow-up can establish the endpoint join without replacing the path.
cases.initialQuestion: Select a two-edge straight path whose site between its endpoints joins the loop's upper corner.
cases.followupQuestion: Does an endpoint of the selected two-edge path join a three-edge loop?

cases.name: Keep the whole original pair
cases.description: Both the path and its original loop are retained. That pair meets at a site between the path endpoints, so an endpoint-contact question answers No. The nearby second loop cannot silently replace the retained loop, although an unrestricted search can find an endpoint join.
cases.initialQuestion: Select a two-edge straight path whose site between its endpoints joins the loop's upper corner.
cases.followupQuestion: Does an endpoint of the selected two-edge path join a three-edge loop?

cases.name: Between with unequal uncalibrated steps
cases.description: The path starts at one loop's upper corner and contacts a second loop at its internal site. The ordered two-edge path places that site between its endpoints. The publication carries incidence and headings, so the follow-up needs no length, equal subdivision or calibration. Only the path is retained; the loop partner may change.
cases.focusLabel: Retained path and its site between the endpoints
cases.initialQuestion: Select a two-edge straight path with an endpoint at the loop's upper corner.
cases.followupQuestion: Does the site between the selected path's endpoints join a three-edge loop?

cases.name: Between with equal uncalibrated steps
cases.description: The path starts at one loop's upper corner and contacts a second loop at its internal site. The ordered two-edge path places that site between its endpoints. The publication carries incidence and headings, so the follow-up needs no length, equal subdivision or calibration. Only the path is retained; the loop partner may change.
cases.focusLabel: Retained path and its site between the endpoints
cases.initialQuestion: Select a two-edge straight path with an endpoint at the loop's upper corner.
cases.followupQuestion: Does the site between the selected path's endpoints join a three-edge loop?

controls.name: Rebuild the reader, retain the observation
controls.purpose: A new induction wrapper over the same observation can use the same retained actual sites and edges.

controls.name: A new observation event
controls.purpose: A lookalike event does not establish identity with the retained observation. The reference stays unsettled.

controls.name: Unfinished capture
controls.purpose: An open selection is not a complete retained context and does not authorize replacement by another matching path.

controls.name: No follow-up search capacity
controls.purpose: Remembering a match does not manufacture an answer when the required follow-up search is unfinished.

controls.name: Retained role absent from the question
controls.purpose: The supplied context and question must agree about the retained role slots. An unadmitted slot is blocked.

limits: These are bounded structural reads over supplied native motif templates. Selecting an actual witness is explicit; the fixture does not learn which interpretation to retain.
Retention fixes the selected roles' actual sites, edge footprint and complete pattern-site correspondence. Unretained roles remain available for another matching partner.
An unrestricted Yes can use another occurrence. A retained No answers about the remembered context; it neither erases that match nor authorizes substitution.
A site between path endpoints is an ordered topological relation. No equal subdivision, length or calibration is required by these questions.
The reference is scoped to one published observation event. A new event remains Open until an explicit correspondence or transfer establishes continuity.
The retained object is a certified interpretation of exposed incidence and headings. It need not recover the author's drawn path grouping when several native walks are valid.
The memory retains its complete proof history. Compact adaptive memory, event tracking, arbitrary pattern discovery and learned selection remain separate work.
Motif matching and correspondence preparation remain eager and bounded. Fewer admissible matches do not by themselves establish a source-side computation saving.
